prompt.context: Bagging Co. makes rolls of grease-proof paper. The production of this paper is unique in that there are many mechanical differences in the production process compared to other paper production lines. In particular, these machines require a larger upfront capital expenditure. Bagging Co. sells this grease-proof paper to bag converters. The bag converters add glue and produce the actual bag of popcorn, then turn around and sell it to major packaged food companies for resale. Recently, the R&D department at Bagging Co. discovered a means to reduce grease soakage by 10x. This is achievable by a relatively simple modification to the current equipment at a negligible cost.
prompt.question: Should Bagging Co. make the new paper?

clarifying_info.q: What is the current cost structure for bag converters?
clarifying_info.a: Bag converters current cost breakdown: $0.30 per 2 sheets, $0.10 per receptor (film applied to bag), $0.05 per popcorn, $0.05 other manufacturing costs — $0.50 total cost.

clarifying_info.q: What is Bagging Co.'s current cost per sheet?
clarifying_info.a: $0.10 per sheet (half fixed cost, half variable cost).

clarifying_info.q: How does grease soakage decrease using single-ply of the new paper?
clarifying_info.a: Grease soakage decreases by 5x with a single-ply of the new paper.

clarifying_info.q: Would bag converters be interested in the new product?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, bag converters like the product. They currently create double-ply popcorn bags and would now be able to create single-ply bags.

framework: Identify profitability drivers for client (Bagging Co.) and client's customer (bag converters)
Assess where value is created along the value chain: end users vs. bag converters vs. novel applications
Quantify economics: analyze cost changes for bag converters switching from 2-ply to 1-ply
Determine Bagging Co.'s cost structure for the new paper and acceptable pricing range
Explore other markets/applications for the new grease-resistant technology

questions.prompt: Where might the value be in this new product? Who benefits?
questions.guidance: Strong answers identify three potential beneficiaries: (1) end users (popcorn consumers) gain a cleaner experience; (2) bag converters gain reduced costs and stronger pricing power vs. non-adopting competitors; (3) novel applications in other markets. Candidate should note end users probably care less (they typically dump popcorn into a bowl), whereas bag converters care more since they can reduce costs or raise prices.

questions.prompt: What is the impact on bag converters' economics when switching from double-ply to single-ply using the new paper?
questions.guidance: Candidate should work through the cost change: old cost was $0.30 for 2 sheets; with single-ply new paper that cost drops. The receptor ($0.10) is eliminated because the new paper's grease-resistance replaces it. New total cost = $0.15 (1 sheet of new paper) + $0.05 popcorn + $0.05 other = $0.25, but the casebook states new total cost is $0.15 to $0.35 range depending on sheet price. At current paper price the bag converter saves significantly, creating incentive to adopt. Adopting converters can squeeze out competition by lowering prices while maintaining strong profit margin.

math.setup: Bag converter old cost: $0.30 (2 sheets) + $0.10 (receptor) + $0.05 (popcorn) + $0.05 (other) = $0.50 total. With single-ply new paper, receptor is eliminated. New cost = price_of_1_new_sheet + $0.05 + $0.05 = price_of_1_new_sheet + $0.10.
steps: New total cost = 1 sheet new paper + $0.10 (no receptor needed)
If sheet priced at $0.15: new total = $0.25 (saves $0.25 vs old)
If sheet priced at $0.30: new total = $0.40 (saves $0.10 vs old)
math.answer: New total cost ranges from $0.25 to $0.40 depending on new sheet price, always below old $0.50 — bag converters benefit at any price up to $0.40/sheet.

questions.prompt: What is Bagging Co.'s current profit margin without the new technology?
questions.guidance: Candidate should use the given cost data: $0.10/sheet cost (half FC, half VC), so $0.05 FC and $0.05 VC. Current sale price to bag converter is $0.15/sheet (implied by $0.30 for 2 sheets). Profit = $0.05/sheet or $0.10/bag. Margin = $0.05/$0.15 = 33%.

math.setup: Current price = $0.30 / 2 = $0.15 per sheet. Current cost = $0.10 per sheet. FC = $0.05, VC = $0.05.
math.answer: $0.05 profit per sheet, $0.10 per bag, 33% margin.

questions.prompt: How should Bagging Co. price a sheet of the new grease-resistant paper?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify the pricing corridor. VC stays at $0.05/sheet. With single-ply production volume per unit unchanged, FC is still $0.10/sheet. Total cost = $0.15/sheet. Price must be above $0.15 (floor = no profit) and below $0.30 (ceiling = bag converter parity with old cost of $0.15/sheet for old paper multiplied by 2). The sweet spot is $0.25–$0.30: above $0.25 Bagging Co. earns more than current $0.05/sheet profit; below $0.30 bag converters still save money.

math.setup: New paper: VC = $0.05/sheet, FC = $0.10/sheet (same fixed base, now spread over single-ply), total cost = $0.15/sheet. Bag converter's current spend on paper = $0.30 for 2 old sheets.
steps: Floor price = $0.15 (cost recovery only, zero profit)
At $0.15–$0.25: Bagging Co. profit < $0.05/sheet current — no advantage for client
At $0.30+: bag converter pays as much or more than current — no advantage for bag converter
Sweet spot $0.25–$0.30: Bagging Co. profit > current AND bag converter still saves money
math.answer: Optimal price range is $0.25–$0.30 per sheet of new paper.

questions.prompt: What other applications or markets exist for this grease-resistant technology?
questions.guidance: Strong answers generate a diverse list across industries. See brainstorming section.

brainstorming.prompt: What are other applications and markets for the new grease-resistant paper technology?

categories.name: Food & Beverage Packaging
ideas: Restaurant to-go boxes and takeout packaging

categories.name: Industrial / Manufacturing
ideas: Auto mechanics industry (wrapping bolts, rings, engine components)
Industrial parts packaging to prevent grease transfer

categories.name: Other Packaging Materials
ideas: Specialty packaging for greasy or oily products
Medical or pharmaceutical packaging requiring grease barriers

recommendation: Yes, Bagging Co. should produce the new grease-resistant paper — the modification is low-cost and the economics are compelling for both Bagging Co. and its customers
Price the new paper in the $0.25–$0.30 range per sheet to capture value while giving bag converters a clear cost advantage over non-adopting competitors
Explore expansion into adjacent markets (food service, industrial packaging) to diversify revenue and maximize the technology's value
risks: Competitors may develop similar grease-resistant technology, eroding pricing power
Bag converters may consolidate or resist adoption if switching costs are high
New markets may require regulatory approval or different product specifications
next_steps: Conduct market research to quantify bag converter willingness-to-pay within the $0.25–$0.30 range
Identify top 2–3 adjacent market opportunities and size them
Pilot the new paper with 1–2 key bag converter customers to validate economics and gather feedback
